title: Oxeye Analytics - rapid prototype & hosting decision discussion
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Intro discovery with Oxeye; they want a rapid prototype to validate latency and cost for a summarization feature. Concerned about PII, want VPC/KMS options. Discussed free credits, quickstart flow, and potential Dedicated pilot. Next step: run a benchmark test with sample traffic and share security docs + pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Head of ML - Oxeye), Samir (CTO), Evan (SRE), Lena (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'll kick us off. can folks say a quick line about what they want to get out of today?
[00:12] Marta: hi, i'm marta. we're trying to get a proof point — a rapid prototype — for a doc summarization flow inside our customer portal. main goals are sub-second-ish latency for short docs, predictable cost, and of course privacy for PII.
[00:27] Samir: and timeline is tight, we'd like something we can demo to internal stakeholders in two weeks.
[00:33] Jordan: great, two weeks is tight but doable for a quickstart. priya, want to cover the hosting options at a high level?
[00:40] Priya: yeah, so redwood exposes the same api across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. hosted is fastest to launch — you get keys, free credits, and you can be calling in minutes. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for throughput predictability, and private gives you VPC/on-prem for data residency and KMS control. important note, some customers start hosted for the prototype and then move to dedicated or private once they need isolation.
[01:05] Marta: quick question — hosted: does it mean our data leaves our vpc? we cannot have that for production.
[01:12] Priya: for hosted yes requests go to redwood's control plane, though we offer short-term options: you can pseudonymize before send, or if you need strict isolation, dedicated with private networking or our private deployment where control plane sits in your VPC. also keys can be managed with your KMS in private.
[01:33] Evan: are there SOC2 / ISO audits for hosted? we need audit logs.
[01:38] Jordan: we are SOC 2-audited, we provide audit logs and token-level billing in the console. i'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:47] Samir: cool. on perf: our expected QPS per user is small but bursty. what's the latency numbers on a 2k token summarize on hosted?
[01:58] Priya: depends on model and quant, but for typical open weights and a 2k token input you'd see 300–700ms per request on optimized paths for short sequences; if you push to dedicated with pinned models and reserved nv8p-like capacity that drops and you also get smaller variance. those numbers are approximate — we'll run a benchmark with your sample payloads to be precise.
[02:20] Marta: sounds good. can we do a smoke test with our real docs?
[02:23] Jordan: yes, we can provision sandbox creds and you can hit the hosted api right away — that's the fastest TTFT. we also give free credits; typically we give a small credit pack for prototyping.
[02:34] Lena: what's the onboarding friction for our SRE to integrate? we use strict egress rules.
[02:39] Evan: yes, our firewall is locked down.
[02:41] Priya: for hosted you'll need to allow outbound to redwood api endpoints, that's trivial. if that's not allowed we can do a private pilot — redwood private runs in your VPC or on-prem, but that requires more lead time. for a two-week demo, hosted + sample masking is the usual path.
[03:00] Samir: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for sustained load?
[03:04] Priya: hosted is usage-based — great for prototypes. for steady high throughput dedicated reserved contracts amortize cheaper per-token costs, and we can show model/quantization recommendations to reduce unit cost. will include a sample cost model in the deck we send.
[03:20] Marta: we heard about automatic batching and KV cache — is that automatic on hosted?
[03:25] Priya: yes, runtime does continuous batching and prefix/KV cache where appropriate; some behaviors vary by model and length distribution. caching helps with repeated prompts or partial histories.
[03:37] Jordan: quick note — i saw 'KV cache' transcribed as 'k v cash' in some places, ignore that, haha.
[03:44] (laughter)
[03:45] Samir: practical: i need to present numbers — can you run a quick benchmark with our sample traffic profile? we'll provide a 48-hour capture of requests.
[03:55] Priya: yes, send sample payloads and we'll run bench on hosted and on a dedicated sim where we emulate reserved capacity. helps to include token distribution.
[04:07] Marta: also we need to ensure PII is stripped. what's your recommended approach for prototypes?
[04:12] Priya: two options: client-side pseudonymization or field-level redaction before calling the API, or use private deployment where data never leaves your network. for a prototype, pseudonymization plus hosted is fastest. for production, private with KMS is best.
[04:29] Evan: we use AWS KMS; can redwood integrate with that?
[04:33] Jordan: yes, private deployments support customer KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. we'll include a KMS integration spec.
[04:41] Lena: can we control model rollouts? e.g., if a new quantized model regresses, we need automatic fallback.
[04:48] Priya: yes, the platform supports rollouts, canary deploys, A/B and automatic fallback to a compatible variant when regressions hit thresholds — we also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets.
[05:00] Samir: ok. how long to get a dedicated pilot up if we decide to start with that instead of hosted?
[05:06] Priya: dedicated provisioning is usually weeks not days — depends on region and capacity. private on-prem is longer. that's why many teams start hosted for the proof then switch.
[05:16] Marta: for the two-week internal demo we want to hit two use cases: single-doc summarize and threaded-conversation extract. is that feasible on hosted?
[05:25] Jordan: yes. we'll: 1) provide sandbox creds & free credits, 2) run a micro-benchmark on your sample payloads, 3) share a short how-to for integrating with client-side masking.
[05:36] (crosstalk)
[05:40] Evan: question on SLOs: do you offer latency SLAs for hosted?
[05:44] Jordan: hosted has best-effort, dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. for production with SLOs, dedicated or private is the way.
[05:53] Samir: any roaming costs for EU data? we have EMEA customers.
[05:57] Priya: redwood has regional endpoints; for hosted we can route regionally. private gives you full control. will include region mapping in the docs.
[06:08] Marta: can we run models ourselves or must we use redwood-provided weights?
[06:12] Priya: you can bring-your-own-model in private deployments; hosted has curated model catalog with verified performance profiles. dedicated can run specific open weights if they are supported by the runtime.
[06:25] Samir: ok let's talk about immediate next steps and ownership.
[06:29] Jordan: here's what i propose: 1) jordan will send the sandbox creds & security pack and a short how-to for masking (today), 2) oxeye sends sample payloads and token distribution for bench (by 2026-03-26), 3) priya runs benchmark (target turnaround 3 business days), 4) jordan to send pricing scenarios for prototype vs dedicated pilot.
[06:50] Marta: that's good. also we will need a short slide for leadership showing cost estimate and security posture.
[06:55] Lena: and samir wants to see KMS integration spec.
[06:58] Jordan: noted.
[07:00] (longer discussion about benchmark specifics and sample formats, inaudible overlap)
[07:35] Priya: one more thing — for the micro-bench we'll measure p50/p95 latency, token cost, and variance; we'll also simulate burst patterns.
[07:45] Evan: perfect.
[07:47] Samir: can you include an example curl and node snippet for the integration?
[07:51] Jordan: yes, we'll include SDK snippets.
[07:54] Marta: thanks everyone.
[07:56] Jordan: ok last quick question from me: what would success look like for the two-week demo?
[08:02] Marta: we want to show: 1) summarization latencies under 700ms median for the 2k token case, 2) acceptable cost estimate for scale (per 100k requests), and 3) proof that PII handling approach meets our security bar.
[08:18] Jordan: great. we'll get to work. i'll follow up with links to the security pack, pricing scenarios, and sandbox creds.
[08:27] (call ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings; e.g., 'dedicated' transcribed as 'dedicate' in a couple places. references: security pack (link sent after call), bench spreadsheet (we'll share gsheet link).
